bull_bear.body:
- Our business is dependent and will continue to depend on our manufacturing facility, and we are subject to certain risks in our manufacturing process.
- Any slowdown or shutdown in our manufacturing operations or strikes, work stoppages or increased wage demands by our employees that could interfere with our operations could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
- We operate from our manufacturing facility situated at Khatwad Tal, Dindori Dist, Nashik, Maharashtra which is spread across approximately 5100 sq. mts.
- The core of our business relies on efficient management of the manufacturing facility, however our operations face several operational risks, some of which are beyond our control, such as the breakdown, failure of equipment or industrial accidents, severe weather conditions and natural disasters.
- Further, we may be subject to manufacturing disruptions due to contraventions by us of any of the conditions of our regulatory approvals, which may require our manufacturing facilities to cease, or limit, production until the disputes concerning such approvals are resolved.
- While we have not encountered significant disruptions at our manufacturing facilities in recent years, we did experience a decline in production during 2020 due to the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic.
- While we have since recovered, we cannot guarantee that future disruptions will not occur.
- Our inability to effectively respond to such events and rectify any disruption, in a timely manner and at an acceptable cost, could lead to the slowdown or shutdown of our operations or the under-utilization of our manufacturing facilities, which in turn may have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations. 2.

risks: Our business is dependent and will continue to depend on our manufacturing facility, and we are subject to certain risks in our manufacturing process.

Any slowdown or shutdown in our manufacturing operations or strikes, work stoppages or increased wage demands by our employees that could interfere with our operations could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We operate from our manufacturing facility situated at Khatwad Tal, Dindori Dist, Nashik, Maharashtra which is spread across approximately 5100 sq. mts.

The core of our business relies on efficient management of the manufacturing facility, however our operations face several operational risks, some of which are beyond our control, such as the breakdown, failure of equipment or industrial accidents, severe weather conditions and natural disasters.

Further, we may be subject to manufacturing disruptions due to contraventions by us of any of the conditions of our regulatory approvals, which may require our manufacturing facilities to cease, or limit, production until the disputes concerning such approvals are resolved.

While we have not encountered significant disruptions at our manufacturing facilities in recent years, we did experience a decline in production during 2020 due to the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic.
While we have since recovered, we cannot guarantee that future disruptions will not occur.

Our inability to effectively respond to such events and rectify any disruption, in a timely manner and at an acceptable cost, could lead to the slowdown or shutdown of our operations or the under-utilization of our manufacturing facilities, which in turn may have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations. 2.

orders_not_placed.note: Affirmative disclosure, verbatim: 'We have considered the above quotations for the budgetary estimate purpose and have not placed orders for them. The actual cost of procurement and actual supplier/dealer may vary.' The statement covers the whole quotation table, so all 12 line items aggregating the printed total of Rs 515.91 lakhs (Rs 514.91 lakhs IPO-funded) are unordered - 100% of the capital expenditure. The Company adds that it has 'not entered into any definitive agreements with any of the vendor and there can be no assurance that the same vendor would be engaged to eventually supply the machineries or at the same costs', that management retains flexibility to change vendor or add/modify/delete machineries at the time of actual placement of order, that no second-hand machinery is being acquired, and that the Promoters, Directors and KMP have no interest in the quoting entities. QUOTATION VALIDITY vs DEPLOYMENT: the RHP states 'Quotation received from the vendor mentioned above is valid as on the date of this Red Herring Prospectus' (cover-dated August 24, 2026), but every quotation validity date falls between September 30, 2026 and October 15, 2026 - i.e. all 12 quotations, and therefore 100% of the Rs 515.91 lakhs capex, expire within about seven weeks of the RHP date while the entire deployment is scheduled across Fiscal 2027 (ending March 31, 2027). The RHP acknowledges the consequence: quotations 'are valid for a specific period of time and may lapse after the expiry of the said period. Consequent upon which, there could be a possible escalation in the cost'. TENSION TO NOTE: an 'Advance already paid - Internal Accruals' of Rs 1.00 lakh is deducted from the Rs 515.91 lakhs total, i.e. an advance has been paid against machinery for which the notes state no orders have been placed; the RHP does not identify which line item the advance relates to. Risk Factor 26 describes the same capital expenditure as 'We have estimated the total cost towards these capital expenditures for Rs 514.91 lakhs', whereas the Objects table prints Rs 515.91 lakhs as the total cost and Rs 514.91 lakhs as the IPO-funded balance.

project.timeline: total_cost_lakhs above is the plant-and-machinery capital expenditure project cost of Rs 515.91 lakhs (the only object with a printed project cost); the aggregate 'Total' of the Objects table is printed as '[●]' because General Corporate Purpose is undetermined until the Issue Price is fixed, so no aggregate project cost is disclosed. Proposed Schedule of Implementation (entire deployment in a single fiscal, Fiscal 2027): Repayment of certain outstanding borrowings Rs 250.00 lakhs; total estimated cost towards procurement of plant and machinery Rs 514.91 lakhs; Funding to meet working capital requirements Rs 300.00 lakhs; General Corporate Purpose '[●]'; the 'Total' row of the schedule table is printed blank. Means of Finance: the entire fund requirement is to be funded from Net Issue Proceeds (printed as '[●]'), hence no firm arrangements of finance under Regulation 230(1)(e) of the SEBI ICDR Regulations are required for 75% of the stated means of finance excluding the proposed issue. Shortfall of funds, cost escalation on machinery (freight, installation, packing and forwarding, customs duty) and any prepayment charges on the borrowings are to be met from internal accruals and/or unsecured loans. No bridge financing has been availed as on the date of the Red Herring Prospectus, though the Company may consider raising bridge financing which would be repaid out of the IPO proceeds. APPRAISAL - affirmative negative statement, not silence: 'None of the Objects have been appraised by any bank or financial institution or any other independent third-party organization. The funding requirements of our Company and the deployment of the proceeds of the Issue are currently based on available quotations and management estimates.' The same is stated under the utilisation table ('...have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution') and in Risk Factor 26 ('these have not been independently appraised by any bank or financial institution'). MONITORING AGENCY - affirmative 'not applicable' on a stated threshold, not silence, and stated consistently in three places: (i) Objects of the Issue, 'Monitoring Utilization of Funds': 'As the size of the offer will not exceed Rs. 5,000 Lakhs, the appointment of Monitoring Agency would not be required as per Regulation 262(1) of the SEBI ICDR Regulations. Our Board and the management will monitor the utilization of the Net Issue Proceeds through our audit committee'; (ii) General Information, 'Appraisal and Monitoring Agency': 'As per regulation 262(1) of SEBI ICDR Regulations, the requirement of monitoring agency is not mandatory if the Issue size is up to Rs 5,000 Lakh. Since the Issue size is below Rs 5,000 Lakh, our Company has not appointed any monitoring agency for this Issue. However, as per section 177 of the Companies Act, the Audit Committee of our Company, would be monitoring the utilization of the proceeds of the Issue'; (iii) Risk Factor 44: 'There is no monitoring agency appointed by Our Company to monitor the utilization of the Issue proceeds... appointment of monitoring agency is required only for Issue size above Rs 5,000.00 lakhs.' No monitoring agency has been appointed and none is claimed to be appointed anywhere in the document - the three statements agree. Ongoing monitoring is instead via the Audit Committee: half-yearly disclosure of application of proceeds under Regulation 32 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, plus an annual statement of funds utilised for purposes other than those stated in the RHP, until the proceeds are fully utilised. Pending utilisation, the Net Proceeds are to be deposited with scheduled commercial banks under Schedule II of the RBI Act, 1934, and the Company confirms the Net Proceeds will not be used for buying/trading/dealing in shares of any listed company, equity market investment, or real estate or real-estate-linked products. Variation of objects requires a shareholder special resolution under Section 27 of the Companies Act, 2013 with an exit opportunity from Promoters/controlling shareholders to dissenting shareholders. The Company also confirms there are no material existing or anticipated transactions with Promoters, Directors, KMP or SMPs in relation to utilisation of the Net Proceeds, and no part of the Net Proceeds will be paid as consideration to them except in the normal course of business. A Statutory Auditor certificate dated August 06, 2026 on utilisation of the loans for the purposes availed has been obtained under Clause 9(A)(2)(b) of Part A of Schedule VI of the SEBI ICDR Regulations.

compliance_legal.risk: Prospective investors should carefully consider all the information in the Red Herring Prospectus, particularly the “Financial Information of the Company” and the related notes, “Our Business” and “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” on page159, 107 and 222 respectively of this Red Herring Prospectus and the risks and uncertainties described below, before making a decision to invest in our Equity Shares.
While we have described the risks and uncertainties that our management believes are material, these risks and uncertainties may not be the only risks and uncertainties we face.
Note: The risk factors as envisaged by the management along with the proposals to address the risk if any.

financial_valuation.risk: Any of the following risks, individually or together, could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations or prospects, which could result in a decline in the value of our Equity Shares and the loss of all or part of your investment in our Equity Shares.

However, we have not experienced any disputes with our customers in the past, there are also a number of factors, other than our performance that could cause the loss of a customer, which include those customers who may demand price reductions, set-off any payment obligations, require indemnification for themselves or their affiliates, or replace their existing products with alternative products, any of which may have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects.

As a result, any failure on our part to maintain applicable standards and manufacture products according to prescribed quality specifications, may lead to loss of reputation of our Company, cancellation of the order, loss of customers, rejection of the product, which will require us to incur additional cost to replace the rejected product, all or any of which could have adverse effect on our business and financial condition.

internal_operational.risk: Our business is dependent and will continue to depend on our manufacturing facility, and we are subject to certain risks in our manufacturing process.

Any slowdown or shutdown in our manufacturing operations or strikes, work stoppages or increased wage demands by our employees that could interfere with our operations could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We operate from our manufacturing facility situated at Khatwad Tal, Dindori Dist, Nashik, Maharashtra which is spread across approximately 5100 sq. mts.

strategy_growth.risk: We derive a portion of our revenues from exports and are subject to risk of international trade.

We have historically derived a significant portion of our revenues from operations from export to countries like: Bahrain, Bangladesh, Cameroon, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Iraq, Kuwait, Lithuania, Mauritius, Nepal, Nigeria, Oman, Poland, Russia, Saint Lucia, Saudi Arabia, Slovenia, South Africa, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey and U.A.E.
Our company is not engaged in any foreign currency hedging.
